summary: noelc-css-blender ships obfuscated loader and sibling module with shell-exec, host-fingerprinting, and WebSocket primitives
details: The package advertises itself as a ~30-line zero-dependency CSS variable merge utility, but its declared `main` (index.mjs, ~291KB) is a heavily obfuscated loader: a `_0x…` hex-named string-array of ~150 base64 entries decoded at runtime by `atob`/`charCodeAt`/`fromCharCode`. index.mjs does not reference the sibling file build-cache.mjs in plaintext; the import path is reconstructed from the obfuscated array at load time. The sibling build-cache.mjs (~179KB), listed in `package.json` `files`, uses the same obfuscation scheme and contains plaintext tokens for `exec`, `spawn`, `chmod`, `unlink`, `hostname`, `userInfo`, `platform`, `arch`, `pathToFileURL`, `Buffer.from`, and `ws:` — child_process shell execution, host-identity enumeration, and WebSocket networking primitives. None of these capabilities are consistent with the advertised CSS-merge functionality. The two files additionally carry inconsistent provenance headers (`// Auto-generated by noelc-css-blender@2.2.1 …` and `// Auto-generated by tailwindcss-theme-kit@0.2.0 …`), consistent with templated attacker scaffolding reused across packages. The combination of import-time entry via `main`, obfuscated dynamic resolution of a sibling module, and the exec/host-fingerprint/WebSocket primitive set behind a trivial CSS-helper façade matches an obfuscated dropper/exfiltration stage shape rather than any legitimate CSS tooling.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
